scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute ticket response times are within the 3‑day SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days), indicating that the surge in tickets is not driven by delayed responses.
The dispute volume rose from 610 tickets in June to 1,260 tickets in September, with a sharp increase in August‑September. This indicates the surge is real and not merely a perception.
Field route completion is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a shortfall in manual meter reads that could lead to estimation and increased dispute tickets.
Among disputed bills, more have ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240), indicating that estimation is not the dominant source of disputes.
The tariff change log contains no recent tariff changes, indicating that tariff modifications are not contributing to the billing dispute surge.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field staff reports a shortage of three readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This indicates that staffing shortfalls lead to missed manual reads and increased reliance on estimation, which could contribute to the dispute surge.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff changes this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not contributing to the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager, indicating a control on dispatch changes.

problem_definition.root_problem: Insufficient manual meter read completion (below 0.95 target) caused by field staff shortage leads to missed or erroneous manual reads, resulting in incorrect bills and a rise in dispute tickets.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Field staff shortage (E-06) reduces manual meter read capacity. → Reduced capacity causes route completion to fall below target (E-03: 0.88 < 0.95). → Below-target completion results in missed or erroneous manual meter reads. → Missed/erroneous reads produce incorrect bills (either via estimation substitution or wrong actual read). → Incorrect bills drive increased dispute tickets (E-02 shows rise from 610 to 1260 tickets).; rejected framings: [('H-REQUESTER-FRAMING', 'Dispute surge is not a response‑speed problem; E‑01 shows response times within SLA (median 1.6\u202fdays, p90 2.8\u202fdays).'), ('H-AMI-READ-ERROR', 'No supporting evidence; E‑05 and E‑07 show no tariff changes and no indication of AMI read errors.'), ('H-HANDOFF-DELAY', 'No supporting evidence; no indication of MDMS‑to‑billing handoff delays or corruption.'), ('H-RULE-CHANGE', 'No supporting evidence; billing import validation rule change log (DA‑RULES) shows no recent changes.')]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-01 deferred to VOB-U-01
